title: U.S. House · Arkansas's 1st District
area: Eastern Arkansas (the Arkansas Delta), including Jonesboro, West Memphis, and Forrest City.

context.text: Both party primaries for this seat were canceled after only one candidate filed in each: incumbent Rick Crawford (R) and Terri Yarbrough Green (D) each advanced unopposed. Steve Parsons advanced as the Libertarian Party nominee from a February 22, 2026 party convention.

candidates.name: Rick Crawford

summary.text: Rick Crawford is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 1st District, first elected in 2010, and is seeking re-election. An Army veteran and former agricultural broadcaster, he has served on the House Intelligence Committee since 2017 and became its chairman in January 2025. He also sits on the Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: Raised in an Air Force family, he lived in various parts of the United States and in England, according to his official biography.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army out of high school and served four years as an Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technician, reaching the rank of sergeant (Ballotpedia lists 1985 to 1989).
Earned a degree in agriculture business and economics from Arkansas State University in 1996; competed in rodeos in college and afterward worked as a freelance rodeo announcer and producer.

Worked in agricultural news reporting and broadcasting, founded and operated the AgWatch Network, a web-based farm news provider serving radio stations in five states, and served as marketing manager for a large John Deere dealer group.

Ran for Congress in 2010 and was first elected that year; Talk Business & Politics reports he was the first Republican to hold the seat since Reconstruction and has won every primary and general election since.
Has served on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence since 2017 and became its chairman in January 2025; previously chaired its CIA Subcommittee.
A senior member of the House Agriculture Committee, he served on the farm bill conference committees in 2014 and 2018 and chaired Agriculture subcommittees in three of his first five terms.

Is vice chairman of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and previously chaired its Highways and Transit Subcommittee; his office credits him with the Interstate 555 designation in Northeast Arkansas.
According to his official biography, he lives in Jonesboro with his wife, Stacy, and their two children, and plays guitar and sings in a band called Triple Nickel.

priorities.text: As a member of the House Committee on Agriculture, says supporting the farm safety net for producers facing crop failure, climate fluctuation, natural disaster, and market downturns is his primary focus in writing the next Farm Bill.

Says insurance companies should be able to sell plans across state lines and supports expanding Health Savings Accounts and Flexible Spending Accounts to give people more control over health care decisions.

positions.summary: Says the Affordable Care Act took control away from patients, raised premiums and deductibles, and should be repealed and replaced with patient-centered health care.
positions.quote: The Affordable Care Act takes control away from patients, has led to higher health care costs, and restricts accessibility to care.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 7296, the SAVE America Act, which requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections and photo identification to vote.
Cosponsored H.R. 722, the Life at Conception Act, which declares that the constitutional right to life is vested in each human being at all stages of life, including the moment of fertilization.

record.text: Has served on House committees during his tenure, including committee assignments renewed each Congress since first taking office in 2011.
Introduced the Cuba Agricultural Exports Act, which would repeal restrictions on financing and marketing that limit U.S. agricultural exports to Cuba.

candidates.researchNotes: No distinct 2026 campaign issues page was found; positions and priorities are drawn from the issue pages and press releases on Crawford's official House site, some of which have not been updated with dated statements in recent years.

candidates.name: Terri Yarbrough Green

summary.text: Terri Yarbrough Green is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 1st Congressional District. A medical pathologist who moved to Northeast Arkansas in 1988 and recently retired, she has not held elected office before and says she decided to run because no other Democrat had filed. She is running on campaign finance reform and universal healthcare, and has also emphasized farm and fuel costs.

background.text: Adopted at birth, according to Talk Business & Politics; describes herself as the daughter of a high school football coach and athletic director.
Graduated from Burges High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Baylor University in 1977; also attended the University of Texas at Arlington.
Received a medical degree from the University of Texas Health Science Center in San Antonio.
Worked as a medical pathologist and moved to Northeast Arkansas in 1988; her Ballotpedia profile calls her semi-retired, and Talk Business & Politics reported in 2026 that she had recently retired.
Has been active with the Greene County Democratic Party and has worked on voter registration, according to Talk Business & Politics; Talk Business lists her as a Democrat from Paragould.
Is running for office for the first time; the Democratic primary was canceled and she advanced to the general election without appearing on the ballot.

priorities.text: Says she is "not a politician" but an ordinary person who will "stand up for the ordinary people" and restore transparency and accountability to Congress.
priorities.quote: I am not a politician, but am an ordinary person, just like you, who believes in service to their country and will stand up for the ordinary people, unafraid of the power brokers.

priorities.text: Lists campaign finance reform and universal healthcare as the public-policy areas she is personally passionate about.
Says dark money should be out of politics and that she believes in free, fair, transparent elections.
priorities.quote: We have to get dark money out of politics. Period.

positions.summary: Listed universal healthcare among the public-policy areas she is personally passionate about in a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (Dec. 2025).
In a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey submission (Dec. 22, 2025), listed raising the minimum wage and tying it to inflation among her policy priorities.
positions.quote: Raising the minimum wage and tying it to inflation.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website (issues listed: accountable government, honest democracy, thriving communities) confirms her minimum wage and healthcare statements; no additional statements on the guide's other issues were found.

candidates.name: Steve Parsons
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party's February 22, 2026 state convention.

summary.text: Steve Parsons (Steven Gene Parsons) is the Libertarian Party nominee for Arkansas's 1st Congressional District and a resident of Lakeview. A consultant and former adjunct professor with a doctorate in economics, he was also the Libertarian candidate for the seat in 2024. He is running on cutting inflation through deregulation and tariff elimination, immigration reform, and reducing incarceration.

background.text: Works as a consultant and has worked as an adjunct professor; Little Rock Public Radio reported in 2024 that he has a doctorate in economics and has taught the subject.
Is a Libertarian from Lakeview, Arkansas, according to Talk Business & Politics.

Advanced from the Libertarian convention as a candidate for Arkansas House District 3 in 2022, and in 2024 was the Libertarian nominee for the 1st Congressional District, receiving 3.1% (8,353 votes) in the general election won by Rick Crawford.

In a 2024 interview, described his political philosophy as centered on limited government, a plain reading of the Constitution and individual choice, and said he was running to give voters options beyond the two major parties.
Advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on February 22, 2026, to the general election ballot.

priorities.text: Cut inflation by eliminating trade tariffs, cutting federal regulations, reducing bureaucracy in visa/green-card processing, and cutting federal spending.
Reform immigration by cutting green-card and work-visa bureaucracy, eliminating tariffs on Latin American goods, and creating a clearer path to legal permanent residency.
Incarceration, substance abuse and mental health reform: says treatment is far more cost-effective than incarceration.

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for eliminating trade tariffs, citing the cost of the 2018 U.S.-China trade war.
positions.quote: Eliminate trade tariffs (the 2018 trade war with China alone costs America $50 billion a year and 166,000 jobs).

statements.quote: The U.S. should eliminate the existing 3/10 rule for existing undocumented immigrants.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website covers immigration, tariffs, regulation, prison reform and foreign policy; on immigration he calls for expanded work visas and a legal path rather than stating a position on enforcement and deportations, so it appears as a statement only.
